newsitem.title: USA: Calvin Grigsby maintains his innocence - attorney.
newsitem.headline: Calvin Grigsby maintains his innocence - attorney.

text.p: The former chairman of Grigsby Brandford and Co Inc, Calvin Grigsby, has not been hiding and is not being sought by authorities, his attorney said late on Friday.
"Mr. Grigsby is not in hiding or missing; nor is he being sought by authorities," Grigsby's high-profile attorney Johnnie Cochran Jr. said in a statement.
"There are no charges pending; and we are hopeful that no charges will be filed, because Mr. Grigsby is not only presumed innocent, but strongly maintains his innocence," Cochran said.

The Miami Herald reported on Thursday that FBI videotapes show Grigsby allegedly offering Dade County, Fla., Commissioner James Burke a $300,000 kickback in exchange for steering a $183 million Dade County bond deal to the firm.

Grigsby resigned from the San Francisco firm Grigsby Brandford and Co, one of the nation's largest minority-owned investment banking firms, on September 17. Grigsby has remained in the San Francisco Bay area, Cochran's office said.

"You may rest assured that we will do everything within our power to see that no charges are filed; and, if they are filed, we will vigorously fight them," said Cochran, who successfully defended O.J. Simpson.
Cochran's statement Friday was the first issued since Grigsby's resignation. Grigsby has not returned repeated phone calls since he left the investment banking firm.
